BiblicalUsage: Gala is milk, and the apostles use it for the first food of faith. Paul fed the Corinthians with milk and not with meat, because they were not able to bear it, in 1 Corinthians 3:2, and he says the same to the Hebrews in Hebrews 5:12: they have need of milk, and not of strong meat. Peter tells newborn babes to desire the sincere milk of the word, that they may grow thereby, in 1 Peter 2:2.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe milk is the right food for the newborn, and the wrong food for the grown. The apostles never despised milk — they fed it gladly — but they expected growth, and I hold that a Christian who still needs only milk has stopped growing.
